ideas.title: Usability-focused feature: how the North Quay bilingual pilot guides readers between English/Polish summaries and Dutch originals
ideas.description: A focused editorial feature that documents the pilot’s current multilingual surface (landing page + six short summaries in English and Polish) while longer interview chapters remain in Dutch; it reports the project’s translation approach (two paid translators; no automated system described), summarizes participation metrics (30 invitations, 9 opens, 4 navigation comments) and the project’s explicit request for navigational feedback, and then (within journalistic limits) lays out concrete navigation clarifications and reader-facing signposting the project can adopt prior to any funded expansion.
ideas.audience: Project editors and managers, the local reading groups and early readers who received invitations or responded, and potential funders assessing whether to support fuller translations.
ideas.rationale: The source reports a limited access pilot that asks for feedback on navigation and shows early, tangible but small engagement; an editorial piece centered on navigation both serves readers who reported confusion and creates a documented account funders and the project team can use when deciding next steps.
ideas.evidence: Landing page and six summaries available in both English and Polish while longer chapters remain Dutch; the project used two paid translators and does not describe an automated system; 30 invitation links were sent and 9 people opened the feedback form with 4 comments about finding their way between summaries and interviews; no reading-comprehension or language-comparison task was carried out; the announcement asks for feedback on navigation and says further languages/full chapters are possibilities for a later funding application rather than promised additions.

ideas.title: Reader-facing bilingual primer (English & Polish) that points clearly to Dutch originals
ideas.description: Publish a concise primer (in English and Polish) that summarizes what is available, explicitly indicates which chapters remain only in Dutch, explains how translated summaries link to originals, and provides step-by-step navigation guidance and an FAQ addressing the navigation confusions reported in the pilot.
ideas.audience: Multilingual community readers (English- and Polish-speaking), local reading groups, and volunteers/helpers who assist readers.
ideas.rationale: Clarifying what is available and how to reach the Dutch originals reduces friction for readers and responds directly to the navigation comments already received.
ideas.evidence: Landing page and six short summaries are now available in both languages; each translated summary links to the original chapter and identifies which text is available in which language; the announcement asks readers for feedback on navigation.

ideas.title: Funder-facing memo: pilot metrics, translation model, and resource considerations to complete full translations
ideas.description: Produce a concise internal memo for potential funders that compiles the pilot’s factual data (which items are translated, the two paid translators and no automated system, invitation/feedback counts, and the lack of formal comprehension testing) and outlines options and potential resource considerations for expanding language coverage or translating full chapters.
ideas.audience: Potential funders, project leadership, and institutional partners evaluating a funding application.
ideas.rationale: The source frames additional language/full-chapter translation as a possibility for a later funding application; a memo that aggregates pilot data will support funding decisions without promising outcomes the project has not committed to.
ideas.evidence: The published account does not describe an automated translation system; the project worked with two paid translators; Thirty invitation links were sent to local reading groups; So far nine people have opened the feedback form, and four have submitted comments; Further languages and full translated chapters remain possibilities for a later funding application.
